places.note: The city God chose for his name to dwell. Site of Solomon's temple, the crucifixion and resurrection, and Pentecost — and the city the prophets say will be made new.
Refuge in famine, then house of slavery — the place God brought Israel out of, the exodus that defines the rest of Scripture.
From the tower of Babel to the empire that burned the temple and carried Judah into exile — Scripture's enduring symbol of proud human civilization.
The river Israel crossed into the promised land, where Naaman was cleansed, Elijah was taken up, and Jesus was baptized.
Lot's descendants east of the Dead Sea. Balaam prophesied here, Israel camped here — and Ruth the Moabite became David's great-grandmother.
Originally the Jebusite stronghold David captured; the name widens through Scripture to mean the temple mount, the city, and finally the people of God themselves.
The empire that destroyed Samaria and deported the northern tribes, then besieged Jerusalem — and was stopped by an angel in one night.
Capital of the northern kingdom, built by Omri. Its fall in 722 BC scattered the ten tribes; by Jesus' day 'Samaritan' was a slur he deliberately overturned.
Esau's descendants, who refused Israel passage and later cheered Jerusalem's fall — the subject of Obadiah's whole prophecy.
The wooded highlands east of the Jordan, known for its healing balm — 'is there no balm in Gilead?'
The land promised to Abraham and his offspring — the whole hinge of the Pentateuch and Joshua.
Where Jacob dreamed of the ladder and said 'surely the LORD is in this place.' Jeroboam later set a golden calf here.
The northern region of Jesus' ministry — despised by Judeans, and where 'the people dwelling in darkness have seen a great light.'
Israel's persistent northern rival (Aram). Naaman its commander was healed; its capital Damascus became the road of Paul's conversion.
The first city taken in Canaan, whose walls fell after seven days. Later, where Jesus healed Bartimaeus and called Zacchaeus down.
Abraham's long home and the burial cave of the patriarchs. David reigned here seven years before taking Jerusalem.
The cedar-covered mountains that supplied Solomon's temple and became the prophets' image of strength and glory.
Ancient capital of Syria — where Paul was struck blind, baptized, and lowered over the wall in a basket to escape.
The rich northeastern grazing land of Og's kingdom — its bulls and oaks are proverbs for arrogant strength.
The Phoenician sea power that supplied cedar for the temple, then drew Ezekiel's oracle against its pride. Jesus healed a woman's daughter in its region.
Destroyed with fire from heaven for its wickedness; the Bible's standing warning, and the city Abraham bargained for.
The southern region around Jerusalem, heartland of the temple and the Sanhedrin.
Saul's hometown and capital, and the site of the atrocity in Judges 19 that nearly destroyed the tribe of Benjamin.
Where Moses fled from Pharaoh, married Zipporah, kept sheep for forty years, and met God in the bush.
The 'house of bread' — where Ruth gleaned, David was anointed, and Micah said the ruler of Israel would be born.
Abraham's first stop in Canaan and Joshua's covenant-renewal site between Ebal and Gerizim. Later the first capital of the northern kingdom.
Named 37 times in Scripture, first at Numbers 21:25.

The great river marking the promised land's ideal northern boundary, and the road Israel's conquerors traveled.

The Philistine city of Goliath, where David once feigned madness to escape.
